subject: Survival model has a nearly singular matrix and INLA crashes

messages.author: 4808110ed3760d39
messages.subject: Survival model has a nearly singular matrix and INLA crashes
parts:
I am estimating a large multilevel, recurrent-event, survival model. I am going to overload you with information incase it is relevant, but in short:

Currently, R-INLA is quitting because the matrix is nearly singular, 

"Fail to factorize Q. I will try to fix it..."

For more details:

Every individual within the dataset regularly shops at a store. At some point they were exposed to my treatment. In total, there are about 2 million people, with approximately 150 million shopping trips (pre and post treatment). I am trying to measure the treatment's effect on their shopping pattern. 

I've begun with a small sample of 700 hundred shoppers (~50,000 trips). I have encoded the data as one row per shopping trip. There is a time-varying, binary flag that indicates when a shopper was exposed to the treatment (0 before exposure, 1 after exposure). 

For the first draft of the model, there is a population level treatment effect and each shopper has an individual-level intercept. The model uses the coxph family. Eventually, I want to include a bunch of customer level features and store level features, but that is after I get this first model to work.

This what the code looks like:

formula = inla.surv(time, status) ~ treatment + f(id, model="iid", hyper = list(prec = list(param=c(1, 1)))) 

mod = inla(formula, family="coxph", data=df, control.hazard = list(scale.model = TRUE), num.threads = 72, blas.num.threads = 72, control.compute = list(openmp.strategy = "huge"), verbose =  TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Survival model has a nearly singular matrix and INLA crashes
parts:
Hi,

It is this issue that a matrix can be numerical singular although not singular. If that happen only for ‘strange’ hyper parameter values its ok, otherwise it has be addressed. I can rerun it here, if you like to check, otherwise its a little hard to ‘debug’. (As its data-dependent). You can email me at he...@r-inla.org unless you want to post on the list. 

For the size of model you’re after, I suggest to look at 

 inla.pardiso()

And register there, as you’ll need that to get going on these large models. …and you cannot use Windows.





H
